newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady on more outages - SEP 24.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady on more outages - SEP 24.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in southeastern U.S. held steady Tuesday against Monday's levels on more outages of generating units in the region, market sources said.
"It was pretty constant," said one East Coast trader, when asked about today's spot price movement in the Southeast.
The effect of cooler temperatures today was mitigated by the shutdown of Florida Power & Light Co's (FP&L) 666 megawatt (MW) Turkey Point 3 nuclear power unit in Florida City, Fla.
FP&L said it hoped to restore Turkey Point 3 back to service later this week.
The utility decided to shut the unit after two control rods fell into the reactor core early Tuesday.
Turkey Point 3 was the third Southeast nuclear units idled in recent days. Florida Power Corp's 825 MW Crystal River 3 remained shut.
Duke Power Co said its 846 MW Oconee unit 2 began dispatch electricity to the grid Wednesday morning. The unit was shut last weekend to repair a leaking valve.

In the Southeastern Reliability Council (SERC), non-firm power for heavy demand hours on Wednesday was quoted near $16.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) for delivery into the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), compared with Monday's range of $15.75-$17.00.
Wednesday peak electricity at southern TVA was valued at $19.25-$20.00, compared with Monday's $20.00 power for Tuesday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, peak, non-firm power was quoted at $20.00-$23.50, flat from Monday's range.
Hourly electricity prices for selective peak hours at the border were assessed at $18.00-$24.00.
